idiom_name: Promise.all over typed async tasks plus a worker_threads pool for CPU-bound work
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's shape: Promise.all (or Promise.allSettled) over async functions is the fan-out and its settlement is the aggregation, with the partial results typed end-to-end; CPU-bound subtasks move to node:worker_threads (typed with @types/node), where each Worker is a real thread and the task boundary is a structured clone, so the message types must be serializable and the worker pool must be sized and terminated. In browser bundles the same structure is a Web Worker pool behind a typed request/response wrapper; the classic master object is unnecessary because promises already carry the partial results.
pitfalls: Promise.all rejects on the first failure while the remaining tasks keep running; allSettled is required to collect per-task failures.
The worker boundary structured-clones: class instances lose their prototype and ArrayBuffers are copied unless transferred, so typed payloads must be plain data.
Workers and their message listeners must be terminated/removed; an abandoned pool keeps the Node process alive.
